instructions: Bring 6 cups of water to a boil in a large pot over high heat. Set 1/2 tsp of the salt aside in a small dish and stir the rest into the water.
Check the edamame bag. If it says they're already cooked, they only need 1 minute in the water.
Add the frozen edamame straight from the bag and stir. Once the water is back at a boil, cook them for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring once or twice, until a bean you pop out is tender with a little bite.
Skim off any foam with a slotted spoon, then drain them in a colander. Don't rinse them, or the salt washes off.
Sprinkle the 1/2 tsp salt you set aside over the hot pods and toss. Leave them for a few minutes to cool down a little.
Serve warm or at room temperature, with an empty bowl for the pods.
method_notes: All three read versions boil frozen pods in well salted water for a few minutes and salt them again once drained. Just One Cookbook uses a lot of salt in the water (4 tbsp Diamond Crystal kosher per quart), cooks them 4 to 5 minutes, skims the foam and says not to rinse, and notes that edamame imported from Japan are precooked and need only a minute. America's Test Kitchen simmers them 3 to 4 minutes and cools them in cold water, and My Everyday Table cooks them in 2 cups of water in a skillet. This one follows Just One Cookbook's ratio for a 16 oz bag. The salt is Just One Cookbook's amount converted to table salt (about half the volume of Diamond Crystal).
